key_insight: Mobile CT, telehealth, and regulated AI are each fairly mature, but their full integration for rural and remote imaging care is still underdeveloped.
clinical_relevance: An integrated mobile CT workflow could improve access to timely imaging, interpretation, and treatment support for patients in rural, regional, and remote settings.
method: Reviewed mobile CT platforms in trucks, trailers, ambulances, and other mobile systems
Examined telehealth technologies that support CT-based care and AI tools for CT with regulatory authorisation or clinical deployment
Compared use across screening/diagnosis, monitoring, risk prediction, and intervention support in multiple body regions and disease areas
evidence_signal: The review synthesises current practice across deployment status, regulatory status, and estimated technology readiness levels, but the abstract does not report new patient outcome data.
watch_item: Real-world adoption is constrained by regulatory variation, connectivity, cybersecurity, workflow integration, and limited evidence of patient-level benefit.
paper_title: Mobile CT Services for Rural, Regional, and Remote Areas: Current Practice and Future Integration with Telehealth and Regulatory-Authorised AI
